model_output.verdict: A senior physical therapist with a clear outpatient rehab specialty and well-described patient work.
write_up: This is a strong physical therapy resume: you name the cases you treat, the patients you see, and the programs you run. The return-to-run line is a model because it says what you built and how many patients completed it.
The main question is how the patient-reported function scores were measured. Your resume isn't likely to be what stands between you and a callback; competition for the role matters too.

cards.line: - Built a return-to-run program that 85 patients completed in 2025
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives your work a name and shows patients completing the program, without making a bigger claim about their recovery.

cards.line: - In 2025, 92% of discharged patients improved their patient-reported function scores
cards.cannot_tell: The improvement is worth showing, but a recruiter can't tell which assessment you used or how many discharged patients the percentage covers.
cards.example: In 2025, 92% of [number] discharged patients improved their patient-reported function scores, measured with [assessment tool]
cards.question: Which assessment did you use, and how many discharged patients were included in the percentage?

fit.note: Your experience points toward outpatient orthopedic physical therapy, especially sports and post-surgical rehab. Mentoring newer therapists and scheduling the PT aide also show senior responsibilities.
